Contract.title: The conformance suite runs its files in parallel and no file dominates a worker, so a full suite run takes a fraction of today's serial time
Contract.Problem: Explicit owner requirement of 2026-11-14: the conformance suite takes too long to run and its length must be cut. A full serial run is recorded at 396.6 seconds (C-0007 run 4, CK2) and measured at 676 seconds under concurrent load on this host; 94 tests sit in six files, the largest holding twenty, so the runner's file-level parallelism cannot engage and every evidence run of every future change pays the whole length. The length is in scratch-repository construction and real CLI spawns, not in case count: reducing the 57 documented cases would cut the framework's core coverage, which the owner's requirement does not ask for.
Contract.Change: The suite's test files are rearranged by topic until no file holds a disproportionate share of the tests, so that a parallel run's wall time approximates its slowest file rather than the sum of all; no test, assertion or helper is changed, added or removed, and a committed baseline of the suite's test titles, taken before the rearrangement, is the reference a check compares against. The test script of package.json runs bun test --parallel, the serial command remains valid, and AGENTS.md states the measured duration of the parallel run. Nothing outside the conformance suite, the test script and that one AGENTS.md line is written.

Constraints.Constraint: The surface grows by nothing: no command, schema, record kind, skill, tool or validation mechanism is added; the change rearranges test files, adds the title baseline beside them, sets the parallel flag in the test script and updates the duration line of AGENTS.md.
Every documented case keeps at least the tests it has today; no case is added, removed, renamed or weakened, and the title baseline check fails on any test the rearrangement loses, renames or adds.

The kernel, CLI, schemas, records, skills, packages and method documents are Protected and untouched; the parallel flag changes no test semantics, and the serial command remains valid without a dedicated re-verification check, the rearrangement being mechanical and type-checked.
No mechanism enters the rationale ledger: parallel execution is the test runner's own flag and the title baseline is a fixture of the conformance suite, not a kernel validation.

NonGoals.NonGoal: No conformance case is added, removed or weakened; the 57 documented cases and today's tests are the fixed inventory, including the six cases whose tests today carry no case id in their titles.
No kernel, CLI, schema, record, skill or package change, and no new tool in src/tools/.
No hard timing threshold in any check: speed is evidenced by the recorded elapsed time of receipts and judged in review, because a machine-dependent ceiling fails on load, not on regression.
No release: the version, the pin, the tag and the migration steps stay as they are (models/architecture/upgrade.md).
No CI sharding and no custom runner: the runner's own parallel flag is the whole mechanism.

Acceptance.Criterion: The whole suite passes under bun test --parallel with the same totals as the serial baseline recorded in C-0007's run 4: 94 tests, one POSIX-only skip, zero failures, 1407 expect() calls.
The parallel run's recorded elapsed time is under half the recorded serial baseline of 396.6 seconds.
The set of test titles after the rearrangement equals the committed baseline exactly: nothing is lost, renamed or added.
The kernel still type-checks: the rearranged files compile and import unchanged.

Automated.Command: bun -e "const fs=require('fs');const path=require('path');const dir='src/conformance';const q=String.fromCharCode(34);const re=new RegExp('test(?:\\.skipIf\\([^)]*\\))?\\(\\s*'+q+'([^'+q+']*)'+q,'g');const titles=[];for(const f of fs.readdirSync(dir).filter(f=>f.endsWith('.test.ts'))){const s=fs.readFileSync(path.join(dir,f),'utf8');for(const m of s.matchAll(re))titles.push(m[1])}titles.sort();const base=fs.readFileSync(path.join(dir,'test-titles.txt'),'utf8').split(/\r?\n/).filter(Boolean).sort();const lost=base.filter(t=>!titles.includes(t));const gained=titles.filter(t=>!base.includes(t));if(lost.length||gained.length||base.length===0){console.error('titles: baseline '+base.length+', now '+titles.length+', lost: '+lost.join(' ; ')+', gained: '+gained.join(' ; '));process.exit(1)}console.log('titles: '+titles.length)"

Decisions.Decision: The owner's requirement is a shorter suite run, not a smaller suite: the length is in scratch-repository construction and real CLI spawns, so the cut comes from parallelism and file arrangement, and the documented case inventory is untouched.
The runner's own file-level parallelism is the mechanism, measured on this host at 396.6 seconds serial (C-0007 run 4) and 230 seconds parallel before any rearrangement, with identical totals.
The largest files are split by topic until none dominates a worker; the split is mechanical and is guarded by a committed title baseline rather than a new validation mechanism.
The test script of package.json runs the parallel form for daily use; the serial command remains valid and is not re-verified by a dedicated check.
No check carries a timing threshold; the speed criterion is the recorded elapsed time of the parallel receipt against the recorded serial baseline, judged in review.
No release: the version, pin, tag and migration steps are untouched; a release remains a separate owner-requested change.
